deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 32% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.1% = 10-year Treasury 5.1% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 42% last year; 27%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

note.headline: AMD drops 5.58% to 504.28, nears support; still above every fair value

summary.thesis: The business is growing faster and earning more, but at 504.28 the price already assumes far more growth than any valuation method in the data supports.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait, because the price is between a support zone and resistance less than one typical daily move away.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38. Swing only on a hold of 480.33–502.6 and a close above 530.13.

note.happening: AMD fell 5.58% to 504.28. It is now below the 517.35–530.13 zone, which acted as support last time and is now overhead resistance. The price sits just above the next support zone at 480.33–502.6, which has been tested 5 times. There is no new news, and the next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
note.business: The business itself did not change today. Only the mood around the stock did. The latest filing, from 2026-11-04, is strong. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, faster than the 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) grew to 7.1B from 5.4B. The company has more cash than debt, with net cash of 8.7B, so its finances are not at risk. Analysts keep raising their numbers: next year's EPS (earnings per share) estimate rose 12.1% in 30 days to 17.69. Two risks are real. First, inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, which means unsold product is building up and could force price cuts that hurt margins. Second, the 17.72% operating margin is near the top of AMD's 5-year range, and peaks like this usually fade. Separately, insiders sold $12.8M outside pre-set plans. That is a governance and sentiment signal, not a change to the business.

worth.text: Every method in the data puts fair value well below the price. A cash-flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 146.48 in the bear case, 187.98 in the base case and 222.62 in the bull case. AMD's own price-to-sales history gives 179.24 to 333.38. Today the stock trades at 18.2 times sales. That compares with a peer median of 13.7 and sits at the 92nd percentile of AMD's own 5-year range. On earnings it trades at 109.9 times trailing EPS but 28.5 times next year's estimate. That gap shows the price leans on next year's earnings showing up. The main reason the methods disagree with the price is the growth assumption. The models cap starting cash-flow growth at 30%, which gives 184.49. The price implies starting free-cash-flow growth of 59.2%. If operating margin fell to 13%, value would drop to 97.39.
worth.key_assumption: Starting free-cash-flow growth: the price implies 59.2%, while the models cap it at 30%, which yields 184.49.
